sections.what_happened: [COUNTED, UNTIERED TRACKER -- hormuz.now, updated 2026-11-07 00:50 UTC] On 6 November 2026, 12 commercial ships crossed the Strait of Hormuz (4 inbound, 8 outbound; 5 tankers). Last 7 days: 62 crossings (29 inbound, 33 outbound), incl. 21 tankers and 0 LNG/LPG carriers. 7-day average 8.9/day, about 10% of the pre-crisis 84.8/day. Most recent crossing detected: OCEAN LEGACY (oil products tanker), inbound, 6 Nov 19:29 UTC. No AIS-visible commercial ship had crossed yet on Nov 7 as of 00:50 UTC. Status: Restricted (since 19 Oct 2026). [PORTWATCH GAP -- STALE] Newest IMF PortWatch snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, stale=true, latest observation 2026-10-18 (4 Hormuz transits, 7-day avg 3.7 vs 2025 baseline 85.5/day). Per prior scans (Nov 6 0000-04/1300-01), hormuz.now counts are ATTRIBUTION-ONLY: the tracker has no declared tier, so its figures CANNOT be used as franchise figures or toward corroboration, and the PortWatch franchise figure is STALE and therefore WITHHELD downstream — narration says what is known without the PortWatch number, and may cite the hormuz.now count only as 'tracker X counts Y'. Do not merge the two series (different methodologies: AIS-visible commercial ships vs PortWatch total transits).
sections.what_verified: Single untiered tracker; no declared-tier family corroborates the Nov 6 count. PortWatch (the franchise counter) is stale. Reported with attribution only.
sections.what_disputed: CENTCOM (via Al Jazeera, Sept 16 mirror — re-date trap, not new) claims the strait 'remains open' and 900M barrels moved since early May; the counted AIS traffic (~10% of normal) contradicts the impression of normal flow. No fresh CENTCOM transit count exists in-window; CENTCOM announcement due 13:30 GMT today (recorded 0400-01).
sections.why_matters: The count, not the claim: 12 ships crossed Hormuz yesterday — against 85 a day before the war.
sections.context: Background: FRANCHISE CHECK (Hormuz by the Numbers) -- hormuz.now Nov 7 update: 12 crossings Nov 6, 7-day avg 8.9/day (~10% of normal); IMF PortWatch still stale

totw_analysis: Our read: The count, not the claim: 12 ships crossed Hormuz yesterday — against 85 a day before the war. The fault line our audience is arguing over: CENTCOM says the strait is open and 900M barrels moved; the counted traffic is ~10% of normal — who is telling the truth about Hormuz?
